key_insight: MediX-R1 enables medical multimodal LLMs to produce clinically grounded, free-form answers by fine-tuning a vision-language backbone with Group-Based RL and a composite, medically-aware reward that enforces semantic correctness and paraphrase robustness.
problem_solved: Existing medical MLLM training/evaluation often relies on multiple-choice or token-level signals and cannot reliably judge semantic correctness or handle paraphrases in open-ended clinical answers, risking inaccurate or unsafe outputs.
method: Fine-tune a baseline vision-language backbone using Group-Based Reinforcement Learning to stabilize and scale open-ended policy updates.

Optimize a composite reward tailored for medical reasoning: an LLM-based binary (YES/NO) accuracy reward for strict semantic correctness plus a medical embedding–based semantic reward to capture paraphrases and semantic closeness.
Train the system end-to-end to generate free-form, clinically grounded answers (beyond multiple-choice) and evaluate using the proposed semantic rewards.
impact: MediX-R1 provides a practical training recipe and evaluation signal for building safer, more accurate medical multimodal assistants that can answer clinicians' free-form questions—beneficial for researchers, benchmark designers, and deployers of clinical AI.
visual_elements: System architecture: vision-language backbone → Group-Based RL loop → composite reward signals (LLM-accuracy + medical embeddings).
Reward breakdown infographic: side-by-side icons/weights for YES/NO LLM accuracy and embedding-based semantic similarity.
Evaluation chart: open-ended answer quality vs. multiple-choice baselines (accuracy, semantic score, safety).
Example panel: input multimodal clinical case → free-form model answer → reward judgments (YES/NO and embedding similarity).
paper_title: MediX-R1: Open Ended Medical Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Sahal Shaji Mullappilly, Mohammed Irfan Kurpath, Omair Mohamed, Mohamed Zidan, Fahad Khan
